correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the one-step kernel from the exponential dwell clocks and rotation by minus one. With b=(1+z²)/2, the incoming weights for targets containing 0 are z, (1−z)+z(1−z)+z²=1, or b+(1−z²)/2=1. The other target classes receive b, z²+(1−z²)/2=b, or z² (including z·z at the corner). At L=3 the three surviving equations are z, 1 and z². Counting weights gives T_L. A full tour can implement any single allowed hop with positive probability and return the frame to its starting orientation. The exclusion configuration graph is connected: reduce the separation to get an adjacent pair, and translate adjacent pairs using two successive hops. This gives uniqueness. Only the two neighbor-blocked states contribute to the signed drift, with opposite signs and weights 1 and z; their difference gives −(1−z)²/T_L. Over a full tour each fixed bond is exposed to each relative phase, so its mean current is v/L times this drift. The limits use z→0, T_L(1)=L(L−1)/2 and 1−z∼p/(2v), and B_L∼L²/4, respectively.
residual_risks: The archived finite diagnostics are not independent replay or the basis of the universal conclusion. Uniqueness and strict sign are asserted only for finite positive rates and the specified two-particle process.

value.rationale: The full finite-ring law is a usable benchmark for closing the moving-defect correlations. It explains the sign by the unequal stationary weights of the two locally blocked configurations, quantifies the coefficient and distinguishes speed and ring-size scalings without mean field. The known qualitative direction is not the contribution.
residual_risks: No inference about higher particle counts, bulk diffusion, or variants of the dwell rule.
